# Vendored contracts of the inference client

The tests of this crate read nothing outside the crate's own tree, so a test that
cannot find its contract fails instead of passing by not running. Every file here is
a byte-for-byte copy of a file that its owner generates, with a sha256 pin beside
it (the sha256 of the file with CRLF normalised to LF). `tests/common/mod.rs`
checks the pin on every read and panics on a missing or altered file. The
repo-level check `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh` fails when a copy
differs from its original (`REQUIRE_CONTRACT=1` also fails when this crate has not
vendored a copy it is listed as a consumer of).

| File | Owner and generator | What the tests do with it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth-core/inference-service-tokens.golden.json` | Auth Core, `apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/inference-service-token.contract.spec.ts` | `tests/token_contract.rs` serves each captured answer to the real client; `tests/real_policy.rs` reads the principal rows and compares them with the compose file |
| `inference-core/infer-statuses.json` | inference-core, `MP_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p inference-core --lib status_contract` in `apps/Model Plane/rust` | `tests/status_contract.rs` decodes every wire status |

Never edit a copy. Regenerate it from its owner, copy the file and its pin here, and
run the crate's tests.

## `auth-core/inference-service-tokens.golden.json`

Written by Auth Core's real mint path: the registry rows for `embedding-engine` and
`graph-index` from `config/plane-service-principals.json`, the real
`authorizePlaneServicePrincipal`, the real organization-binding check, the real tenant
posture resolver (org-core is the only double, and it enforces service authentication
as `auth-core-org-core-retention-posture.contract.json` says) and the real
`ConvexTokenService` that signs the RS256 JWT. Each case holds the request, the HTTP
status and body Auth Core answered, and the decoded header and claims.

- The tokens are the real compact JWTs, except that the signature segment is replaced
  by a fixed marker. The signing key is ephemeral, so a real signature would change
  on every run and bury every real change in noise. The client does not verify
  signatures (inference-core does).
- Time is frozen (`frozenNowSeconds`); the tests move a manual clock relative to it.
- The cases cover every posture a registry row can carry: `persistent`, `zdr`, and
  `tenant` with both values of the organization's setting, plus the typed 503
  answers (`retention_posture_unavailable`, `organization_directory_unavailable`) and
  the 403.
- `registry` is the two committed principal rows. `tests/real_policy.rs` compares them
  with the Control Plane file when it is reachable, and Auth Core's spec does too.
  Regenerate this golden whenever those two rows change; the real-policy test
  tells you when it is stale.

Regenerate (also vendors the copy and writes both pins):

    cd "apps/Control Plane/auth-core"
    UPDATE_CONTRACT_GOLDEN=1 npx jest inference-service-token.contract

then put the new digest in `GOLDENS` in `scripts/tests/zdr-contract-sync.test.sh`.
Regeneration is byte-identical when nothing changed.

## `inference-core/infer-statuses.json`

Every way an Infer, CreateEmbedding or modality call can fail on the wire (the gRPC
code, the `x-mp-provider-error` kind, the retry timing), generated by inference-core
from the code that builds its statuses. It has no pin beside the original; the digest
is pinned in `GOLDENS` in the sync script, and the pin here is checked by this
crate's tests against this copy.
